title: Label Reliability and Study-Level Leakage Bound Measurable Performance in T-Cell Epitope Immunogenicity Prediction

creators.name: Terano, I Nyoman Agung Ananda
creators.affiliation: Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia

description:
Code, curated benchmark and analyses for the manuscript of the same name.

Computational predictors of CD8+ T-cell epitope immunogenicity report ROC-AUC of 0.85–0.90 on data derived from the Immune Epitope Database. This deposit measures how much of that reflects transferable biology and how much reflects the structure of the benchmark itself.

  • Holding out data by peptide, the standard precaution in this field, lowers AUC by only 0.014 relative to random splitting (IEDB 0.826 vs 0.840; on the independent TRAP dataset peptide grouping scores above random). Grouping by source publication reduces AUC to 0.607. Sequence similarity is not the cause (similarity-grouped splits score 0.82), the pattern holds for logistic regression and within single assay families, and about 60% of the gap comes from one all-negative study.
  • A baseline using allele identity alone, with no peptide information whatsoever, reaches 0.752 and outscores every published predictor tested.
  • Two published predictors were trained on 37.5% and 27.1% of the evaluation pairs; on pairs neither had seen, no predictor's interval excludes chance.
  • Agreement between laboratories assaying the same peptide–HLA pair is κ = 0.273, bounding measurable performance at AUC 0.636.

Contains the evaluation protocol, the curated 31,274-pair benchmark with both peptide- and study-grouped split schemes, all model predictions, and the outputs of the audited third-party predictors so the comparisons can be reproduced without installing them.
